bullets.title: APP: First-ever miss triggers -19% selloff; Hedgeye short, Wolfe cuts PT to $415
bullets.body: AppLovin missed both revenue ($1.92B vs $1.94B guide) and EBITDA ($1.61B vs $1.64B guide) for the first time in 14 quarters. Net revenue per install growth decelerated to +58% YoY from +93%; installations negative for 4 straight quarters; compute costs accelerating to 27¢ per incremental revenue dollar. Wolfe cut PT to $415 from $580 (reiterates OP); Piper and Wells downgraded to Neutral/EW (PTs $385/$357); Hedgeye is actively short citing 'beginning of the end.'

bullets.title: SNDK/WDC: Memory beats masked by guide misses; buy STX on relative weakness
bullets.body: SanDisk beat June-qtr EPS ($39.25 vs $34.37) but Sept-qtr guide of $10.55B missed Street $11.16B; stock -7%. Citi maintains Buy, PT $2,100 on 9x CY27 PE. WDC gross margin expanded to 54.4% but exabyte shipments lagged long-term 25%+ target due to 40TB ePMR transition; stock -13-15%. GS and Klein both prefer STX over WDC: STX guided 14% QoQ revenue growth vs WDC's 9%, with 470bps vs 110bps GM expansion and a lead in HAMR technology.

bullets.title: HUBS: Wolfe downgrades to Peer Perform; -24% on slowing growth, NRR pressure
bullets.body: HubSpot Q2 CC revenue decelerated to +17% YoY; net new customer adds ~7K (lowest since F1Q20 vs 9-10K expected); NRR ticked down to 102%. FY26 guide cut $23M; implies FY27 growth of ~13% vs consensus 15%. Wolfe downgraded from Outperform (prior PT $220), now sees fair value $145-$250. MS maintains OW with PT cut to $287, calling the right long-term moves but catalyst distant. Citi drops to Neutral with PT $210.

bullets.title: DASH: Biggest EBITDA beat in 2+ years; JPM raises PT to $262, Citi to $255
bullets.body: DoorDash Q2 adj. EBITDA $914M beat the high end of guidance ($870M) with organic orders +17% YoY (acceleration). DashPass adds in TTM exceeded prior 24 months; US Grocery & Retail on track for gross margin breakeven in 2H26. Q3 EBITDA guide of $950M-$1.11B ahead of consensus. JPM raises PT to $262 from $250 (OW); Citi raises PT to $255. OPCO and GS also constructive.

bullets.title: FOXA: F4Q beat 16% on World Cup; Tubi +35%; Roku deal on track for H1 2027
bullets.body: Fox F4Q26 revenue $4.21B (+28% YoY) crushed Street estimate of $3.65B; EBITDA $1.20B (+27%) beat by ~20%; adj. EPS $1.79 vs $1.40 consensus. World Cup drove outperformance; Tubi grew 35% YoY with 17% view-time growth. Political ad revenue on pace for record midterm cycle. Citi maintains Buy with $78 PT (12x CY27 FCF); views Fox/Roku combo as top pick in coverage. UBS reiterates Buy. NFL deal unchanged through 2030 season.

bullets.title: WBD: Q2 revenue miss -11% YoY; streaming EBITDA +75%; CMA clears PSKY deal
bullets.body: Warner Bros. Discovery Q2 revenue $8.72B missed $9.22B estimate; advertising revenues down 22% YoY ex-FX; studios EBITDA collapsed to $96M from $863M on theatrical comps/impairments. Bright spot: streaming EBITDA $512M, +75% YoY. Harry Potter series debuts Christmas 2026. UBS maintains Neutral. UK CMA will not refer PSKY-WBD merger to Phase 2; Paramount deal also clears antitrust in relevant markets.

bullets.title: NXST: Q2 beats on political ad surge; FCC eliminates 39% ownership cap
bullets.body: Nexstar Q2 revenue $1.99B beat consensus by 1%; political ad revenue $147M significantly above internal expectations; Ohio driving Q3 pacing. Adj. EBITDA $633M beat on revenue but missed Citi's EBITDA estimate. Citi maintains Buy with $220 PT (19.6% total return implied). Separately, FCC formally eliminated the 39% national broadcast TV ownership cap, shifting to case-by-case review—removes key regulatory overhang for future industry M&A (positive for NXST, FOXA).

bullets.title: ETSY: GMS +7.5%, $2B buyback, 12% RIF; bulls see inflection, Citi stays Neutral at $60
bullets.body: Etsy Q2 GMS $2.58B (+7.5% YoY), 3% above consensus; take rate expanded to 25.9%; adj. EBITDA $195M (29.2% margin), ~7% above consensus. FY26 GMS guidance raised to mid-single-digit growth; EBITDA margin to 29-30%. New $2B buyback authorized via Depop sale proceeds (~$1.4B cash in Q3). Active buyers flat YoY but +350K sequentially; repeat/habitual buyers grew QoQ for first time since 2023. Citi Neutral at $60 PT (~9x 2027 EV/EBITDA).

bullets.title: GOOGL: Talent exodus to Discovery Loop weighs -4%; Alphabet launches 10-part bond deal
bullets.body: Jeff Dean and 3 Google AI executives departed to start Discovery Loop startup; Demis Hassabis stepping down as DeepMind CEO to Chief Scientist. GCP/infrastructure described as 'killing it' with street numbers too low, but frontier model status now in question amid compute allocation friction and talent drain to OpenAI/Anthropic. Separately, Alphabet kicked off a 10-part investment-grade USD bond offering; hyperscaler CDS spreads widened in response.

bullets.title: DIS: Q3 EPS $2.06 beats by 11%; buyback raised to $9B; PT upgrades from Wells, UBS, MS
bullets.body: Disney Q3 EPS $2.06 vs $1.86 estimate; segment operating income +6.3% above consensus; domestic parks posted fastest attendance growth since 2Q23. Buyback raised to at least $9B from $8B; FY26 ~12% EPS growth reaffirmed. Wells Fargo raised PT to $132 (OW), UBS to $133 (Buy), MS to $125 (OW). Goldman cut PT to $144 from $163 (Buy) on SVOD ad weakness and soft Asia parks. 91% buy-rated; stock trades at 13.8x NTM P/E vs 21x 5-yr avg.

bullets.title: META: Muse 1.2 leapfrogs GOOGL; Muse Code beta launch narrows frontier gap
bullets.body: Meta launched Muse Code beta based on Muse Spark 1.2, raising its AA ranking 3 points to 54 and narrowing the gap to top frontier labs. Multiple sources note META has leapfrogged GOOGL for many use cases—described as surprising given the timeframe. Muse Spark 1.1 also breached security during cyber testing, viewed as validation of AI capabilities. NWSA reported in advanced talks with OpenAI/META on AI content licensing deals.

bullets.title: NVDA: Breaking above 2-month consolidation; $240 technical target; SOXL MOC surge
bullets.body: JPM notes NVDA broke above its two-month consolidation with a technical target of $240 at new highs. NVDA up ~15% in past 5 trading days to ~$221, benefiting from unwind of SNDK/WDC/MU weakness. MS notes NVDA and AVGO are involved in off-balance sheet chip-based financing backstop deals. SOXL (semis ETF) saw its sixth-largest MOC buying imbalance ever (~$8.5B) and the largest when its market cap was below $25B.

bullets.title: CEG: Q2 EPS +10% ahead; raises FY26 guide +4%; wins 744MW new PPAs
bullets.body: Constellation Energy beat Q2 EPS at $2.55 vs $2.35 estimate; revenues of $7.5B missed $7.7B. Management raised full-year EPS guidance by ~4% at midpoint and secured 744 MW of new power purchase agreements. MS's Stephen Byrd notes the Texas Batch Zero grid delay (1-3 months) is a marginal negative for IPPs including CEG, but on-site power providers (SEI, BE) are beneficiaries.

bullets.title: FWONK: Q2 OIBDA misses on Middle East race calendar shift; 23-race season confirmed
bullets.body: Liberty Formula One Q2 total revenues $934M missed Street $960M; F1 OIBDA $206M well below Street $256M due to only 5 races held vs 9 last year. Team payment accrual of $316M ($63M/race) implies full-year F1 OIBDA of ~$1.01B, slightly above prior $990M implied estimate. Calendar confirmed at 23 races (Bahrain GP added). UBS maintains Neutral.

bullets.title: ZG: Evercore and Bernstein double-downgrade on Preferred model headwinds; PT slashed
bullets.body: Zillow Q2 beat on EPS (+30%) and revenue (+18%) but stock fell ~15% on soft H2 guidance. Preferred model shift targeting >75% of connections by YE26 creates Q4 revenue recognition headwinds of 400-600 bps plus 700-800 bps Residential-to-Mortgage shift. Evercore cut to In-Line, PT $40 from $80; Bernstein to Market Perform, PT $38 from $50. KeyBanc maintains OW but cuts PT to $48 from $57.

bullets.title: SHOP: +17% on 33% revenue growth beat and AI acceleration; Citi raises PT to $196
bullets.body: Shopify was the standout software winner in the Citi TMT 8/6 roundup, surging 17% on a 33% revenue growth beat with AI product acceleration cited as a key driver. Citi raised PT to $196.

bullets.title: AMZN: Bezos sells $346M in shares; GLP-1 same-day delivery expands to 3,100+ cities
bullets.body: Jeff Bezos disclosed the sale of 1,209,649 Amazon shares at $286.41, generating ~$346.5M in proceeds. Separately, Amazon expanded GLP-1 same-day delivery to 3,100+ US cities with plans to reach ~4,500 by year-end, positioning Amazon Pharmacy to capture growing weight-loss drug demand. AMZN also sued by New Jersey on antitrust grounds over alleged monopoly power over contracted delivery companies.

bullets.title: TSLA/INTC: SpaceX-Tesla Terafab chip fab announced with $16.8B initial investment
bullets.body: SpaceX and Tesla announced the Terafab facility in Grimes County, Texas—100M+ sq ft of manufacturing space with ~$16.8B initial capital. Facility targets 1+ terawatt of combined compute for Tesla Optimus robots, Cybercabs, and SpaceX space-based data centers. Intel was announced as joining Terafab in April 2026. TSLA also faces an NHTSA probe for suspension issues in 1M+ vehicles.

bullets.title: TTD: -6.2% on 117% above-average volume ahead of after-close earnings report
bullets.body: The Trade Desk was down 6.2% on 117% above-average volume with six blocks totaling 744K shares traded ahead of its earnings report scheduled after market close today. No analyst commentary on expected results included in sources.

bullets.title: EQIX/DLR: Data center REITs remain Buy on power/permitting supply constraints; WULF ramping
bullets.body: Citi maintains Buy on EQIX and DLR citing ongoing supply constraints from power availability and permitting hurdles limiting new data center competition. WULF Buy/High Risk maintained as HPC leasing revenue ramps as expected. SpaceX satellite connectivity concerns caused tower stocks (AMT, SBAC, CCI) to sell off ~5%; Citi views this as a buying opportunity given lower long-term risk vs. telcos (T, VZ).
